To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glass transition temperature (and hence stiffness) of the resins is reduced upon incorporation of acrylated epoxides of vegetable oils.

(i) the glass transition temperature of VE was lowered with incorporation of acrylated epoxides of vegetable oils, but urethane crosslinking restored the glass transition temperature; (ii) incorporation of acrylates of epoxidised vegetable oils reduced the fracture toughness and energy of the vinyl ester resin, but the effect was not significant when the resin was urethane crosslinked; (iii) incorporation of acylated epoxides of epoxidised soy and linseed oils reduced
VE was successfully modified with AESO and AEOL and the crosslink density of VE could be enhanced by adding polyurethane crosslinks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new vinyl ester resins modified with functionalised vegetable oils.
the development of a novel class of vinyl ester resin hybrids with enhanced thermal and mechanical properties.
the effect of additional urethane crosslinking and the effect of different vegetable oils on the mechanical, thermal and fracture properties of vinyl ester resins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VEUH modified with AESO and AE LO is a good candidate for the production of structural composites.
AES(L)O modified VE and VEUUH are suitable for applications where the thermal degradation resistance is not a major issue.
VEUH was the best performer in terms of Tg, fracture properties, and thermal stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of AES(L)Os reduced the glass transition temperature of the parent VE and VEU, and that the thermal stability of the parent resins decreased with increasing content of AES(L)OS.
the incorporation of acrylated epoxides from vegetable oils into bisphenol A vinyl ester resins reduced the glass transition temperature of the hybrids.
the incorporation of AESO and especially AELO in the parent VE resin was not beneficial in terms of the mechanical and thermal properties of the resins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tg of a vinyl ester resin can be enhanced by urethane crosslinking and by incorporating acrylate epoxidised soy and linseed oils.
the Tg of VEUH can be enhanced by blending with AES(L), but this does not improve the fracture toughness.
the incorporation of acrylated epoxide vegetable oils (AESO/AELO) into VE resin does not improve its mechanical properties.
